title: Acute Stress Disorder - Criteria
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Criteria

CORE ALIASES: Acute stress reaction, ASD, post-trauma acute symptoms.

DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA:
A. Exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence in one (or more) of the following ways: 1. Directly experiencing... 2. Witnessing... 3. Learning that... 4. Repeated or extreme exposure...
B. Presence of nine (or more) of the following symptoms from any of five categories (Intrusion, Negative Mood, Dissociation, Avoidance, Arousal), beginning or worsening after the traumatic event(s) occurred:
- Intrusion: recurrent memories, nightmares, flashbacks, distress at cues, physiological reactivity.
- Negative mood: persistent inability to experience positive emotions.
- Dissociative: altered sense of reality, inability to remember aspects of trauma.
- Avoidance: of memories/thoughts/feelings or external reminders.
- Arousal: sleep disturbance, irritability, hypervigilance, concentration problems, exaggerated startle.
C. Duration of the disturbance is 3 days to 1 month after the traumatic event(s).
D. Clinically significant distress or impairment.
E. Not attributable to substance or medical condition.

REQUIRED FEATURES: Trauma exposure (Criterion A) + 9+ symptoms across clusters + 3 days to 1 month duration.

RULE-OUTS / DIFFERENTIALS: PTSD (symptoms persist >1 month), Adjustment Disorder (stressor not meeting trauma A criterion), Dissociative disorders, Substance intoxication/withdrawal.

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: "No trauma exposure", "symptoms started years ago", "chronic not acute".

PROVENANCE: DSM-5-TR. Guideline: APA strongly recommends trauma-focused CBT if symptoms persist.
